topics.topic: Whether open_store accepts a missing database path and creates it or requires an existing path
questions: Must open_store permit an absent database path by treating FileNotFoundError from os.lstat as safe before creating the database, or must the database already exist so os.lstat can find it?
Must open_store require the database path to exist so os.lstat can find it, or must it permit an absent database path and create the database file?
Must a missing database path be accepted so SQLite can create the database, or must os.lstat successfully find an existing non-symbolic-link database before SQLite is opened?

judgement.why: The topic asks the same question as P1 on the same unchanged passages.

precedent.topic: Whether open_store may create a missing database file or requires an existing database
quotes: then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link;

Every file and directory the module creates inside data_directory — the database file and its journal, the content-addressed area, the spool area, each run's spool directory, every temporary and every published file — MUST be created owned by the process's effective user and granting no permission to group or others, so that the privacy check of the next start passes on the kernel's own files (A18 rule 2).
precedent.why: The text anticipates creation of the database file but does not say how the required pre-open os.lstat handles a path that does not yet exist.
